artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A virtual knot diagram is a generic immersion of a circle in the plane with each double point marked either as a classical crossing (with over/under information) or as a virtual crossing (a small circle), considered up to the generalized Reidemeister moves (classical Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3, the purely virtual moves V1, V2, V3, and the mixed move). A long virtual knot is the analogous notion for a generic immersion of an oriented line that agrees with the standard horizontal embedding outside a compact set, considered up to the corresponding long versions of the generalized Reidemeister moves. A flat virtual knot (resp. long flat virtual knot) is the equivalence class obtained by forgetting the over/under information at every classical crossing (so each classical crossing becomes a transverse flat crossing), modulo the analogous flat Reidemeister moves.

A biquandle is a set X with two binary operations a^b and a_b satisfying axioms equivalent to invariance under the generalized Reidemeister moves, so that the set of biquandle colorings of a virtual knot diagram gives a virtual knot invariant. There is a "long-knot" enhancement of biquandle/quandle invariants in which the two endpoints of a long virtual knot are decorated by distinguished elements, producing stronger invariants of long virtual knots than of their closures.

For a long flat virtual knot F, the descending diagram construction D(F) is defined by traveling along F from its incoming endpoint and, at each flat classical crossing, declaring the first strand encountered to pass over the second; this turns each flat crossing into an ordinary classical crossing and produces a long virtual knot D(F). The class of D(F) depends only on F, so for any virtual knot invariant I, the assignment F ↦ I(D(F)) is an invariant of long flat virtual knots.

Problem. Develop a strengthening of the invariant theory of long virtual knots and long flat virtual knots that simultaneously:
(a) extends the long-knot biquandle/coloring invariant framework by combining the long-virtual-knot constructions with biquandle structures so as to produce invariants strictly stronger than those currently known;
(b) extracts from the long-knot framework new invariants of classical (long) knots that are not derivable from existing classical invariants; and
(c) uses the descending-diagram construction F ↦ D(F), together with the resulting invariants I(D(F)) for varied choices of virtual knot invariant I, to make progress toward a complete classification of long flat virtual knots up to flat equivalence.

Either produce such invariants with explicit calculations distinguishing long flat virtual knots not separated by previously known invariants, or prove that the resulting family of invariants {I ∘ D : I a virtual knot invariant} is a complete invariant of long flat virtual knots.
artifact.status_search_result: No source found establishing a full classification of long flat virtual knots, nor a definitive strengthening that resolves the combined long-knot/biquandle program. Related work (e.g., parity biquandle invariants, affine index polynomials, and biquandle decorations of long virtual knots) provides partial progress and stronger families of invariants, but the broader classification and the combined-invariant program remain active areas. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Virtual Knot Theory and Combinatorial Knot Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Compendium of open problems in virtual knot theory including classification questions for flat virtual knots and long virtual knots.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of (long) flat virtual knots is listed as an unsolved problem.

status_evidence.title: Parity Biquandle Invariants of Virtual Knots
status_evidence.snippet: Parity cocycle invariants distinguish virtual knots not distinguished by corresponding non-parity invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Strengthenings of biquandle invariants in the virtual setting continue to be developed, indicating the program is ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Bridging colorings of virtual links from virtual biquandles to biquandles
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to refine biquandle-type invariants for virtual links.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research, no completed classification of long flat virtual knots.
